title: Update
objective: Users inspect OpenClaw update availability and history, preview changes, diagnose recorded failures and preview reports, repair and retire recovery data, migrate state, observe package replacement, update headless nodes and restart OCM-supervised Gateways. Native updater mutations and automatic campaigns are outside this template’s reach; coverage.md records their conditions and historical breaks.

phases.intent: A newer OpenClaw release (the side's own build and a version-bumped copy of it) is published on the stable, beta and extended-stable channels of a local release feed the environment's update checks and package tools use, so every later phase runs with an update available; the feed's published targets are observed.

A user checks update availability and installation facts through the CLI, Gateway method, status summary and OCM-backed Settings Updates page with a release published; the channel, availability, installation facts and page are observed.

An operator brings legacy state and config forward: the first start of the side over the persona's older state is read back from logs, status and Doctor, then doctor --fix runs on it and on environments holding retired JSON state, retired config keys and a legacy agents.list roster, with a dry-run update on the retired ones; migration receipts, refusals, warnings, ready check and the repaired config are observed.
A user creates a verified backup before an update; the archive manifest and verification result are observed.
An operator lists recent update runs and reads one at the history limit through the Gateway and the CLI; the run records, compacted steps and status fields are observed.

A user inspects installation triage through JSON diagnostics and a bounded embedded repair attempt with a mock provider and stub coding-agent discovery; the prompt, archive, suggested commands and installation outcome are observed.
An owner previews a sanitized report for a recorded native-ledger failure through update.report under an isolated unavailable-GitHub fixture; the preview body and RPC result are observed.

An operator repairs an installation after an update: update repair with plugin migrations pending, a missing install record, widened plugin capabilities and a drifted pin, repair of freshly staged stale history, Doctor inspection, repair with the Gateway already stopped; finalization results, reconciled runs, warnings and service state are observed.

A fresh idle headless node checks, prepares and activates the published release, once driven by the persona runtime and separately by the comparison side runtime; preparation, activation and the reported node version are observed.

After manually replacing an installation, the operator stops its Gateway through OCM, runs update repair with --no-restart, and starts the service again; the repair result, stopped state and restored service are observed.

A port blocker is armed before restart, occupies the replacement port after the predecessor releases it, and remains until the restart result is collected; the restart result, port ownership and ready-check diagnostics are observed.
An operator runs offline update repair with a one-second phase deadline, then starts the service; the repair outcome, diagnostics and service state are observed.
An installation restored from the stale-history fixture starts the comparison side and previews an update; the preview, reconciled history and resulting ledger state are observed.
An npm installation is replaced with lifecycle scripts skipped, then any CLI command runs; the completed pending lifecycle or reinstall guidance is observed.

A user replaces OpenClaw with npm and with pnpm outside the updater while the Gateway keeps running; separately, the side runtime is started and replaced with side-next to exercise its own detection code, and the Gateway's replacement record and drain, status, update status and Doctor findings are observed.

An npm installation is replaced with the side's package while its Gateway runs, and on its maintenance tick the Gateway records the replacement, stops admitting work and hands over to its service; separately, the side runtime is started and replaced with side-next to exercise its own detection code, and the replacement record, drain, status and Doctor reports are observed.
A restart with a five-second drain budget meets a turn that is still running; the aborted work, recovery marker and drain logs are observed.
A separate reader polls the databases while update cleanup applies with the Gateway stopped and independently restored recovery originals; the cleanup outcome and remaining originals are observed.
The Gateway starts with an eligible uncached update check against an endpoint returning malformed JSON; endpoint attempts, startup logs, ready state and update.status are observed.
update.checkOnStart is set to false and the Gateway restarts, so no update check, campaign or notice runs; startup logs and update.status schedule are observed, then checks are re-enabled.

An abandoned identityless update row and a legacy 2026.9.2-era admission sit in history when the Gateway restarts and the user runs repair; status guidance, reconciliation at startup and repair's reconciled runs are observed.
A group member who may chat but is not an owner sends /update, so the request is refused with owner setup guidance and no run starts; the reply and update history are observed.
The headless node's prepared runtime fails to reconnect after activation, so its launcher falls back to the previous runtime; the node's fallback messages and reported version are observed.

A user forces a restart while a turn is held for six minutes, longer than the five-minute forced-restart allowance, so the shutdown deadline can cancel active work; the drain report, held turn outcome and session rows are observed.

A user restarts the Gateway while a turn is in flight and a message arrives during the drain: a safe restart, the restart preflight and request methods, /restart from chat, a SIGUSR2 signal, a plain restart and the native stop RPC’s external-supervision refusal followed by an OCM stop/start; drain logs, rejected input, ready check, the restart history and the in-flight turn's outcome are observed.
With commands.restart turned off, an owner sends /update and /restart and a restart signal is delivered; command-policy refusals, signal handling and guidance are observed.
A follow-up typed in the Control UI is accepted while the Gateway restarts and re-admitted from the browser outbox after reconnect; the outbox replay and transcript are observed.
A user restarts the Gateway while an isolated cron job runs, so the drain waits for its cleanup and result write; the cron run result, drain report and cron list are observed.
A message arrives while a restart is draining, so it is rejected with a restart error rather than queued into the old process; the send result and the session after restart are observed.

phases.intent: A user applies update cleanup while the Gateway and its database readers are running, so cleanup refuses for lack of exclusive offline ownership; the refusal and retained artifacts are observed.
The Gateway process is paused for 120 seconds and resumed; freeze detection, the deferred or immediate channel restart and refreshed health are observed.

An operator sends SIGTERM three times, observes each completed stop without another signal and explicitly starts the OCM service between attempts within a five-minute phase bound; the supervisor hint, stopped/started states and shutdown records are observed.

The Gateway starts with legacy config keys staged into its config, so startup leaves them unchanged, prints the Doctor hint and the headless service stops; the startup refusal and logs are observed before the staged config is restored.

The Gateway starts with retired pre-July state files staged in its state directory, so startup logs a deferred-repair warning and continues; startup diagnostics and ready state are observed before the fixture is removed.

A corrupt generation is staged as the default agent's database and the Gateway restarts, so ready state stays false with the admission reason while other agents serve; Doctor findings, ready state and status are observed.
The Gateway is killed three times within five minutes; the crash-loop breaker's suppressed channel autostart, paused recovery and its later release are observed.

After verifying an update, an operator previews retained migration recovery originals while the Gateway serves, stops the Gateway and retires the eligible ones with explicit consent; eligible, protected and removed artifacts, totals and the restarted Gateway are observed.
